summary: Douglas County, WA 18-foot L-4 lookout built 1941 on Badger Mountain; the cab was moved to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center in 1999 and is displayed there.

facts.design: 18-foot treated timber tower with a standard Plan L-4 lookout cab

access.note: Lookout interiors are open only during center events or by special arrangement (CBFIC). WTA describes three short trails at the center; no entry fee

visit.trail_note: At the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center north of Entiat; the Washington Trails Association lists no entry fee and dogs on leash

events.note: Build year per the FFLOS register. The NRHP nomination describes a Plan L-4 revised 1932 and says the original site is undocumented
Lookout house moved onto the Badger Mountain summit from an unrecorded original site; a 1947 Forest Service letter names Badger Mountain as a previous move
Oscar Richardson began as lookout in 1953; the NRHP says he ended in 1972 and the FireLookout.com list says 1974
Manned during the 1988 Dinkelman Fire; the fire could be monitored from the site
Listed 12/27/1990 as part of the USDA Forest Service Fire Lookouts on Wenatchee NF multiple property listing; the listing describes the original summit site
Cab moved to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center at Entiat
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register 20 August 2012

corrections.why: The FFLOS register dates the move of the cab to 1999. It says only the cab moved, so the relocation may not cover the whole tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and the record give 1941. The NRHP nomination describes a Plan L-4 revised in 1932, says the lookout house was moved onto the summit from an undocumented site, and says the land was donated around 1941. Its 1947 letter names Badger Mountain as a previous move. The sources do not agree on when the house was built, so 1941 is kept with that caveat.

The FireLookout.com list runs Oscar Richardson to 1974, the NRHP nomination says 1972, and the FFLOS says the tower served the forest until the 1980s. The manning during the 1988 fire is recorded, so unstaffed is dated to the 1980s with this caveat.

sources.title: Badger Mountain Lookout, National Register of Historic Places nomination (NRIS 90001915)

notes_for_editor: The NRHP listing (NRIS 90001915, 12/27/1990) describes the lookout on its original Badger Mountain summit. This record links it to the Columbia Breaks site, where only the cab is said to be displayed, so the listing may not describe the current exhibit. The kind 'ground' on this record is not confirmed by any source read. The NRHP says the summit was donated around 1941, while the FFLOS dates the build to 1941; the house's build date and move date are not settled. Parent record us-wa-badger-mountain (status relocated) was not edited.
